question: What will happen if resistance is measured in a powered circuit?

options.text: The resistance value will be higher than expected.
The test leads will heat up.

solution:
__**Explanation:**__

The multimeter may get damaged.

Measuring resistance in a powered circuit using a multimeter is a common mistake that can lead to severe consequences, including damaging the multimeter itself. To understand why this happens, let us delve into the fundamental workings of resistance measurement and the precautions required when using a multimeter.

**Why Measuring Resistance in a Powered Circuit is Harmful:**

When you attempt to measure resistance in a powered circuit, the following issues arise:

 
• **External Voltage Interference:** The external voltage from the powered circuit can combine with the voltage supplied by the multimeter. This can lead to incorrect resistance readings because the multimeter cannot distinguish between the voltage it generates and the external voltage.
 
• **Excessive Current Flow:** The external voltage may cause a surge of current through the multimeter’s internal resistance measurement circuit. This can exceed the design limits of the multimeter, causing overheating or damage to its internal components.
 
• **Damage to Multimeter Components:** Multimeters are designed with specific voltage and current tolerances. When these limits are exceeded due to measuring resistance in a powered circuit, the sensitive internal components, such as fuses or input protection circuits, can be damaged.

**Precautions to Avoid Damage:**

To prevent damaging the multimeter or obtaining incorrect readings, follow these precautions:

 
• Always ensure the circuit is powered off before attempting to measure resistance.
 
• Discharge any capacitors in the circuit to eliminate residual voltage.
 
• Verify the multimeter’s settings and ensure it is set to the resistance mode before proceeding.

**Conclusion:**

The multimeter may get damaged if resistance is measured in a powered circuit due to external voltage interference and excessive current flow. Always adhere to proper safety practices and ensure the circuit is powered off before performing resistance measurements
